text:
sarah_support: Customer onboarding stuck — trial grant blocked by fraud/abuse checks (case CR-10923). Promo code was applied but trial not activated. Customer reports they used their company email originally but signed up from a VPN. Can someone take a look? acct_id: acct_12345

matt_risk: pinging @kevin_engineer for logs. also posting to risk queue. any quick indicators?

fraud-bot: Automated fraud check summary (id: FC-9221) — score: 82. Flags: disposable_email=1 (email domain tempmail.io), ip_proxy=1 (IP 198.51.100.23 AS12345 proxy), card_velocity=2, geo_mismatch=1. Recommendation: manual review / hold.

kevin_engineer: I pulled the audit. Promo apply returned 403 FRAUD_HOLD, rule=email_disposable. Command I ran: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://internal.api/accounts/acct_12345/flags` — output indicates `email: raj@tempmail.io`, `ip: 198.51.100.23`, `promo_code: ONBOARD50`.

sarah_support: Customer says they actually have a corporate address raj@startup-example.com but used a backup tempmail to complete signup while on a coffee shop VPN. They pasted screenshots of the promo code on the checkout page and a picture of their company ID. Asking if we can do a manual override to unblock onboarding.

matt_risk: We can do a temporary override after verifying identity. Two options: 1) ask them to re-register with corporate email and re-run checks, or 2) grant a 48h trial override and require CS follow-up to collect verification. Which do we want?

olivia_cs: From CS perspective, low friction is better — grant 48h so they can experiment and we can get them into product. We'll request proof (company email or copy of company email header) during the session. 

kevin_engineer: If risk approves, I can flip a flag `account.meta.trial_override=true` and re-run the enrollment job. Example patch we use: ```PATCH /internal/accounts/acct_12345 {"trial_override":"48h","override_by":"matt_risk","reason":"customer provided ID and claims corporate email"}``` Will log audit entry.

matt_risk: Ok doing quick verification — checked company domain WHOIS and LinkedIn, looks legit. I will apply a manual override for 48h and create an audit ticket. @kevin_engineer go ahead when I confirm.

fraud-bot: Action queued: manual_override request by matt_risk. Waiting for engineer apply.

kevin_engineer: Applied override: audit OV-20260401-7745, set `trial_override=48h`, triggered re-eval of promo. Promo apply now returned 200 TRIAL_GRANTED. Snippet: ```{ "acct":"acct_12345", "promo":"ONBOARD50", "status":"trial_granted", "expires_at":"+48h" }```

matt_risk: Manual override applied. Note: record for post-mortem — user registered using disposable email while on a proxy. We'll add a follow-up rule to surface corporate-email claims when signups use known disposable domains.

olivia_cs: Messaging customer now: "We granted a 48-hour trial while we confirm your company email. Please reply with your company email or a screenshot of a company email header and avoid VPN during re-registration. We'll confirm and extend if valid."

sarah_support: Customer replied "Thanks — I see the trial active now, will share company email in thread." Closing the immediate blocker. Leaving ticket open for verification. :thumbsup: 

matt_risk: Thanks team. After verification, if domain checks out we'll revoke the manual flag and update the audit. If they fail verification, we'll revoke the trial and note in policy.

kevin_engineer: Logged all changes in infra audit (OV-20260401-7745) and created follow-up ticket INT-468 to add a lightweight prompt during signup when disposable domains are detected.

sarah_support: Closing case CR-10923 for now; will re-open if customer doesn't provide proof. 

olivia_cs: Noted — I'll leave a CS task to contact customer in 24h.
